subtopics: Theme variables versus ordinary CSS variables
Keeping theme definitions at the appropriate scope
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of understanding the @theme directive.
Apply one appropriate technique to a small Tailwind CSS example.
Verify the expected result and identify a common failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on understanding the @theme directive and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding the @theme Directive helps a team reuse visual decisions without losing flexibility for real application interfaces.

content_blocks.title: Module 14 learning map
content_blocks.alt_text: Four-step module learning map: Introduction to Tailwind CSS Theming → Spacing and Sizing Tokens → Extending the Default Theme → Theme Architecture for Real Products. Lesson pages add code examples and practice.
content_blocks.caption: Learning map for Module 14, from the opening concept to a practical checkpoint.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: Theme variable syntax; Defining custom values; Generating utilities from theme namespaces; Theme variables versus ordinary CSS variables; Keeping theme definitions at the appropriate scope. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.expected_output: Theme tokens define reusable brand color and radius values that can map to utilities.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to understanding the @theme directive, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Complete the linked practical exercise “Theme customization”. Define two brand tokens in @theme and use the generated utility names in a small component.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to understanding the @theme directive.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to understanding the @theme directive.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: Theme tokens define reusable brand color and radius values that can map to utilities.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying understanding the @theme directive without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Understanding the @theme Directive is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
